CashPilot Version 2: "CashPilot Pro"
The AI-Powered Financial Command Center for Small Business
What It Is
CashPilot Pro is an intelligent financial analysis platform that sits on top of your accounting and payment data, combining real-time data synchronization with a proactive AI analyst that continuously monitors, explores, and advises on your business finances. It is the financial intelligence module of what was previously envisioned as "The Helm" — scoped specifically to the financial domain, with all of the AI sophistication (exploratory analysis, tax-grounded RAG, persistent memory, multi-entity consolidation) but none of the scope sprawl that made The Helm unshippable. The spreadsheet remains the primary data viewing interface, but CashPilot Pro adds a conversational AI interface (sidebar, companion app, or chat integration) and a backend intelligence engine that operates autonomously — finding insights, monitoring risks, and surfacing opportunities without being asked.

Who It's For
The same small business owners as Lite, but specifically those who:

Manage multiple LLCs or business entities
Have tax optimization needs (especially crypto-related accounting)
Want the AI to proactively find issues and opportunities, not just answer questions
Need grounded, cited financial and tax advice — not generic LLM guesses
Are willing to pay $49-99/month for a tool that replaces hours of manual analysis and potentially saves thousands in missed tax optimizations
This is also the version you build toward for the commercial SaaS product.

The Problem It Solves
CashPilot Lite solves the data assembly problem — getting financial data into a usable format without manual work. CashPilot Pro solves the financial intelligence problem — understanding what the data means, what it implies, and what you should do about it. Small business owners aren't just overwhelmed by data collection; they're overwhelmed by interpretation. They don't know which tax deductions they're missing, whether their cash flow trajectory is dangerous, whether a seemingly profitable deal actually loses money after taxes and fees, or which of their three LLCs is quietly bleeding cash. A human CFO would catch these things. CashPilot Pro provides CFO-level analysis at a fraction of the cost — grounded in actual tax code, actual financial data, and actual business context, with every insight cited and confidence-scored.

The Three-Tier AI Analysis Engine (Detailed)
This is the core differentiator of CashPilot Pro. Each tier operates differently and serves a different purpose:

TIER 1: Structured Playbooks (Automated, Daily)

These are deterministic, rule-based analyses that run every time data syncs. They don't use an LLM for detection — only for narration. They are reliable, cheap, fast, and predictable.

Playbook	What It Checks	How It Works	Example Output
Cash Flow Forecast	Projected cash position 30/60/90 days out based on AR/AP aging, recurring revenue/expenses, and historical patterns	Python time-series analysis on transaction history + current AR/AP	"At current burn rate, LLC #1 will be cash-negative in 38 days unless Invoice #4051 ($12,400, 22 days overdue) is collected."
Anomaly Detection	Any metric that deviates significantly from its historical baseline	Statistical z-score analysis on spending categories, revenue lines, transaction sizes	"Office supplies spend ($3,400) is 280% above your 90-day average ($890). Investigate: 3 transactions to new vendor 'TechEquip LLC' totaling $2,800."
Margin Analysis	Revenue vs. COGS by product/service line, customer profitability	SQL aggregation + comparison against historical margins	"Service line 'Tax Preparation' margin dropped from 62% to 41% this quarter. Primary driver: contractor costs increased $8,200 with no corresponding price increase."
AR/AP Health	Overdue invoices, payment trend deterioration, concentration risk	Aging bucket analysis + trend detection on payment timing	"Client 'Meridian Holdings' has slowed payment from avg 18 days to 47 days over 3 months. They represent 31% of your receivables. Risk: High."
Tax Liability Tracker	Estimated quarterly tax obligations based on YTD income	Rule-based calculation using configured tax rates and entity types	"Estimated Q2 federal tax liability: $14,200. State (FL): $0. Self-employment: $3,800. Next estimated payment due: June 15."
Expense Trend Monitor	Month-over-month and category-level expense growth	Comparison analysis with configurable thresholds	"Total operating expenses grew 14% MoM while revenue grew 3%. Top growing categories: Software subscriptions (+$1,200), Contractor payments (+$3,400)."
Revenue Concentration	Dependency on top customers/revenue sources	Pareto analysis on revenue by customer/source	"Top 3 clients represent 67% of total revenue. If any one churns, monthly revenue drops below breakeven."
After all playbooks run, the LLM receives the aggregated findings and generates the plain-English summary for the AI Summary tab. The LLM narrates; it doesn't detect. This keeps Tier 1 fast, cheap, and deterministic.

TIER 2: Exploratory Agent (Autonomous, Weekly + On-Demand)

This is the "go find things I didn't think to look for" capability. It's an LLM agent with SQL tool access and RAG retrieval over the tax/legal knowledge base.

How one exploration cycle works:

Step 1: ORIENT
────────────────
The agent receives:
  • High-level business context (entity type, industry, size, state)
  • Summary statistics (revenue, expenses, cash, key ratios)
  • This week's Tier 1 findings (so it doesn't duplicate)
  • Its own prior findings from the last 4 weeks (so it doesn't repeat)
  • The database schema (so it knows what tables/columns exist)

Step 2: HYPOTHESIZE
────────────────────
The agent generates 5-8 hypotheses worth investigating.
These are NOT pre-programmed — the LLM decides what to look at.

Example hypotheses the agent might generate:
  • "Revenue is up but profit is flat — let me check if there's a 
     specific cost category eating the growth"
  • "I notice 3 refunds this month to the same customer — let me 
     check if this is a pattern or one-time issue"
  • "Let me check if there's a day-of-week pattern in sales that 
     could inform cash flow timing"
  • "The business has significant crypto transactions — let me check 
     if any trigger wash sale implications under current IRS guidance"
  • "Let me look at vendor payment terms vs actual payment timing 
     to see if we're leaving early-payment discounts on the table"

Step 3: INVESTIGATE
────────────────────
For each hypothesis, the agent:
  a) Writes a SQL query against the PostgreSQL database
  b) Executes it (via a controlled SQL execution tool)
  c) Examines the results
  d) Decides whether to drill deeper (write another query) or move on
  e) If tax/legal context is needed, queries the vector store 
     (pgvector) for relevant tax code sections

SECURITY CONSTRAINT: The agent has READ-ONLY database access.
It can SELECT but never INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE.

TOKEN OPTIMIZATION: The agent queries the database locally. 
Only the result sets (not raw data) go to the LLM. A query 
that scans 50,000 transactions might return a 10-row summary 
table — only those 10 rows enter the LLM context.

Step 4: SYNTHESIZE
───────────────────
The agent produces a ranked list of findings:

  FINDING 1 (High Confidence):
  "Your Stripe processing fees have increased from 2.7% to 3.4% 
   of revenue over the last 6 months. This is costing an additional 
   $420/month. Cause: 38% of transactions are now international 
   cards, which carry a 1% surcharge."
  [Source: Stripe transactions table, fee analysis]
  [Recommendation: Consider Stripe's IC+ pricing plan]

  FINDING 2 (Medium Confidence):
  "Based on your YTD income trajectory and current entity structure 
   (single-member LLC), you may benefit from S-Corp election for 
   next tax year. Estimated savings: $4,200-6,800/year in 
   self-employment tax."
  [Source: P&L data + IRC §1362 + IRS Rev. Proc. 2013-30]
  [Recommendation: Discuss with tax advisor before March 15 deadline]
  [⚠️ TAX ADVICE — VERIFY WITH PROFESSIONAL]

  FINDING 3 (Low Confidence):
  "Sales volume appears to dip ~20% in the first week of each month 
   across the last 4 months. This could be coincidental (small sample) 
   or could indicate a billing cycle dependency worth investigating."
  [Source: Transaction timestamps, weekly aggregation]
  [Recommendation: Monitor for 2 more months before acting]

Step 5: STORE + DELIVER
────────────────────────
  • All findings stored in the AI insight log (PostgreSQL) with 
    timestamps, confidence scores, and source queries
  • Top findings pushed to the spreadsheet "AI Insights" tab
  • High-priority findings (confidence: high + impact: high) 
    optionally sent via email or Slack
  • Findings become part of the agent's memory for next cycle 
    (so it builds on prior discoveries, not repeats them)
The Tax Optimization Example (Your $4,000 vs. $3,000 Sale Scenario):

This is how it would actually work in the Tier 2 agent:

Agent examines a pending or recent $4,000 sale → 
  Queries the tax knowledge base (pgvector RAG):
    "What are the tax implications of $4,000 additional 
     income for a [entity type] in [state] given YTD 
     income of [amount]?"
  
  Retrieved context: 
    IRC §1(j) tax brackets, state tax tables, 
    self-employment tax rates, QBI deduction thresholds
  
  Agent calculates:
    $4,000 sale → $X marginal federal tax + $Y SE tax 
    + $Z state tax = $2,000 total tax burden → $2,000 net
  
  Agent then tests alternatives:
    $3,000 sale → $A marginal federal tax + $B SE tax 
    + $C state tax = $500 total tax burden → $2,500 net
  
  Agent identifies that the $3,000 price point keeps 
  income below a threshold that triggers higher rates.
  
  Output:
    "⚠️ Tax Optimization Opportunity: The pending $4,000 
     sale to [Client] would net $2,000 after estimated 
     taxes ($2,000 in combined federal/state/SE tax at 
     your current marginal rates). However, pricing at 
     $3,000 would net $2,500 due to remaining below the 
     [specific threshold] bracket. Net benefit: +$500.
     
     [Source: YTD P&L + IRC §1(j) + State Tax Code §X]
     [Confidence: Medium — depends on no other income 
      changes this quarter]
     [⚠️ TAX STRATEGY — VERIFY WITH TAX PROFESSIONAL]"
TIER 3: Conversational Q&A (On-Demand, User-Initiated)

The user asks a question → a query router classifies what's needed → the system retrieves relevant data via SQL + optionally RAG → the LLM generates a cited answer.

This is identical to CashPilot Lite's Q&A, but enhanced with:

Persistent conversation memory: "You asked about Vendor X last week — here's an update"
RAG access: Can ground answers in tax code when relevant
Deeper data access: Can write ad-hoc SQL queries, not just pull pre-defined reports
Follow-up awareness: Understands context from the current conversation
Action suggestions: "Would you like me to add a recurring alert for this?"
The Tax & Legal Knowledge Base (RAG System)
What gets embedded and stored in pgvector:

Content Category	Source	Update Frequency	Volume
Federal tax code (relevant sections)	IRS.gov / Cornell LII / eCFR	Quarterly or when laws change	~100-200 chunked sections
IRS Publications (334, 505, 535, etc.)	IRS.gov PDF → parsed text	Annual	~50-100 chunks per pub
State tax codes (relevant states)	State revenue department sites	Annual	~50-100 chunks per state
Crypto tax guidance	IRS Notice 2014-21, Rev. Rul. 2019-24, subsequent guidance	As issued	~30-50 chunks
Self-employment / entity structure guidance	IRS publications + professional summaries	Annual	~50-100 chunks
Sales tax / nexus rules	State-specific, Stripe reporting guides	Annual	~50-100 chunks
CashPilot's own analysis history	Generated by Tier 2 agent	Continuous	Grows over time
Business-specific context and preferences	User-provided during onboarding and conversations	As provided	~20-50 chunks per company
Total initial knowledge base size: ~500-1,000 chunks. This is small — pgvector handles this trivially. No need for Pinecone or dedicated vector infrastructure.

How RAG retrieval works in practice:

User question or Agent hypothesis involves tax/legal context
    ↓
Extract key terms: entity type, income level, state, topic
    ↓
Generate embedding of the query
    ↓
Similarity search against pgvector (top 5-10 chunks)
    ↓
Retrieved chunks are added to the LLM context along with 
the financial data
    ↓
LLM generates answer grounded in both data AND cited law
    ↓
Output includes: [Source: IRC §199A] or [Source: IRS Pub 535, Ch. 11]
Critical guardrails for tax/legal content:

Every tax-related output is tagged with [⚠️ TAX ADVICE — VERIFY WITH PROFESSIONAL]
Confidence scoring distinguishes "straightforward code application" from "requires interpretation"
The knowledge base has a last_verified date on every chunk — stale content is flagged
The system never says "you should do X" for tax strategies — it says "based on [cited code], option X may result in [estimated outcome]"
Multi-Entity Support
CashPilot Pro supports multiple companies from a single installation:

Database structure:

Every table has an entity_id column
A master entities table maps companies with metadata (name, type, state, EIN, QBO connection, Stripe connection)
An entity_relationships table tracks inter-company transactions
The AI is always aware of which entity it's analyzing and can compare across entities
Spreadsheet structure (two options, configurable):

Option A: One spreadsheet per entity + one "Consolidated" spreadsheet that aggregates across all entities
Option B: One master spreadsheet with entity-prefixed tabs (LLC1_PL, LLC2_PL, CONSOLIDATED_PL)
AI multi-entity capabilities:

Consolidated financial summaries across all entities
Side-by-side entity comparison
Cross-entity anomaly detection ("LLC #2's expenses grew 3x faster than LLC #1 — same vendor appears in both")
Inter-company transaction tracking and reconciliation
Entity-specific tax optimization (different entity types have different tax implications)
Conversational Interface Options
Since the team hasn't decided on the UX format, here are the options ranked by build complexity:

Option	Description	Build Effort	UX Quality
A: Spreadsheet tab	Type in cell, response in adjacent cells (same as Lite)	Low	⭐⭐ Functional but clunky
B: Simple web chat	Standalone web page with chat UI, hosted alongside the backend	Medium	⭐⭐⭐ Clean, familiar
C: Google Sheets sidebar	Custom sidebar panel within Google Sheets using Apps Script	Medium	⭐⭐⭐⭐ Integrated, professional
D: Excel add-in (taskpane)	Custom ribbon button opens a chat panel inside Excel	Medium-High	⭐⭐⭐⭐ Integrated, professional
E: Slack/Teams bot	Chat with CashPilot in your existing messaging tool	Medium	⭐⭐⭐ Convenient, contextual
Recommendation: Start with Option B (simple web chat) for fastest build, then add Option C or D (spreadsheet sidebar) as a polish step. The web chat can be built in a day with a React/HTML frontend hitting your existing FastAPI backend.

Security Architecture
Layer	Implementation
Data at rest	PostgreSQL with encryption at rest (AES-256). Managed PostgreSQL services (e.g., Supabase, Neon, Azure Database) handle this by default.
Data in transit	TLS/HTTPS everywhere — API calls, spreadsheet syncs, LLM requests
LLM data exposure	Minimize what goes to the LLM: send aggregated summaries and query results, not raw transaction dumps. Anonymize PII where possible (replace customer names with IDs in analytical queries). Use Azure OpenAI for enterprise data protection guarantees.
API credentials	QBO/Stripe OAuth tokens encrypted in database, never logged, never sent to LLM. Token refresh handled automatically with error alerting.
Access control (internal)	Single-user for now. When multi-user: role-based access at the entity level (Owner sees all, Bookkeeper sees assigned entities only).
Access control (future SaaS)	Full tenant isolation: separate database schemas or row-level security per tenant. No cross-tenant data leakage possible. SOC 2 Type II compliance before external launch.
Audit logging	Every AI query, every data sync, every insight generated is logged with timestamp, user, entity, and data accessed.
Backup	Daily automated database backups with 30-day retention.
Tech Stack
Component	Technology	Reasoning
Backend	Python (FastAPI)	Same as Lite — best ecosystem for all integrations needed
Database	PostgreSQL + pgvector extension	One database for both relational and vector data. Simplicity.
Spreadsheet sync	Google Sheets API (gspread) → add Excel (Microsoft Graph) in Phase 2	Google Sheets first for speed
LLM	Azure OpenAI (GPT-4o) primary, Claude API fallback	Azure for compliance; model-agnostic design so you can switch
Embedding model	OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (via Azure)	Best price/performance for the volume needed
Agent framework	LangChain or custom ReAct loop	Tier 2 agent needs tool execution (SQL + RAG). LangChain accelerates this, but a custom loop is simpler and more controllable. Evaluate during build.
Hosting	Railway or Azure App Service	Railway for speed; Azure if compliance requires it
Scheduling	APScheduler or Celery (if task queue needed)	Daily syncs, weekly agent runs, periodic token refresh
Chat UI	Simple HTML/JS page or Streamlit	For the companion chat interface — don't over-invest here
Build Timeline
Phase	Timeline	What's Delivered
Phase 1	Weeks 1-3	CashPilot Lite (as described above) — working internal tool with QBO sync, spreadsheet dashboard, basic AI Q&A
Phase 2	Weeks 4-6	Tier 1 playbooks (all 7), weekly AI summary with insight narration, Stripe integration, anomaly alerting
Phase 3	Weeks 7-10	Tax knowledge base curation + pgvector RAG pipeline, Tier 2 exploratory agent (basic version — 3 exploration cycles per run), conversational chat interface
Phase 4	Weeks 11-14	Multi-entity support, Tier 2 agent refinement (persistent memory, longer exploration chains), confidence scoring and citation system, security hardening
Phase 5	Weeks 15-18	Polish, testing across multiple real companies, edge case handling, documentation, decision on SaaS architecture
CashPilot Pro internal v1	~4.5 months	Fully functional AI-powered financial command center for internal use across multiple entities
Estimated Running Costs (Internal Use, 3-5 Companies)
Item	Monthly Cost
Hosting (Railway/Azure)	$20-50
PostgreSQL managed (with pgvector)	$15-30
Azure OpenAI API (Tier 1 narration + Tier 2 agent + Q&A)	$50-150
Embedding API (for RAG)	$5-10
Google Sheets API	Free
QBO/Stripe APIs	Free
Total	$90-240/month
For context: DataRails would cost $500-2,000/month plus a $10,000-50,000 setup fee for comparable AI financial analysis. CashPilot Pro delivers 80% of that capability for under $250/month in infrastructure costs.

AR/AP Health	Overdue invoices, payment trend deterioration, concentration risk	Aging bucket analysis + trend detection on payment timing	"Client 'Meridian Holdings' has slowed payment from avg 18 days to 47 days over 3 months. They represent 31% of your receivables. Risk: High."
Tax Liability Tracker	Estimated quarterly tax obligations based on YTD income	Rule-based calculation using configured tax rates and entity types	"Estimated Q2 federal tax liability: $14,200. State (FL): $0. Self-employment: $3,800. Next estimated payment due: June 15."
Expense Trend Monitor	Month-over-month and category-level expense growth	Comparison analysis with configurable thresholds	"Total operating expenses grew 14% MoM while revenue grew 3%. Top growing categories: Software subscriptions (+$1,200), Contractor payments (+$3,400)."
Revenue Concentration	Dependency on top customers/revenue sources	Pareto analysis on revenue by customer/source	"Top 3 clients represent 67% of total revenue. If any one churns, monthly revenue drops below breakeven."
After all playbooks run, the LLM receives the aggregated findings and generates the plain-English summary for the AI Summary tab. The LLM narrates; it doesn't detect. This keeps Tier 1 fast, cheap, and deterministic.

TIER 2: Exploratory Agent (Autonomous, Weekly + On-Demand)

This is the "go find things I didn't think to look for" capability. It's an LLM agent with SQL tool access and RAG retrieval over the tax/legal knowledge base.

How one exploration cycle works:

Step 1: ORIENT
────────────────
The agent receives:
  • High-level business context (entity type, industry, size, state)
  • Summary statistics (revenue, expenses, cash, key ratios)
  • This week's Tier 1 findings (so it doesn't duplicate)
  • Its own prior findings from the last 4 weeks (so it doesn't repeat)
  • The database schema (so it knows what tables/columns exist)

Step 2: HYPOTHESIZE
────────────────────
The agent generates 5-8 hypotheses worth investigating.
These are NOT pre-programmed — the LLM decides what to look at.

Example hypotheses the agent might generate:
  • "Revenue is up but profit is flat — let me check if there's a 
     specific cost category eating the growth"
  • "I notice 3 refunds this month to the same customer — let me 
     check if this is a pattern or one-time issue"
  • "Let me check if there's a day-of-week pattern in sales that 
     could inform cash flow timing"
  • "The business has significant crypto transactions — let me check 
     if any trigger wash sale implications under current IRS guidance"
  • "Let me look at vendor payment terms vs actual payment timing 
     to see if we're leaving early-payment discounts on the table"

Step 3: INVESTIGATE
────────────────────
For each hypothesis, the agent:
  a) Writes a SQL query against the PostgreSQL database
  b) Executes it (via a controlled SQL execution tool)
  c) Examines the results
  d) Decides whether to drill deeper (write another query) or move on
  e) If tax/legal context is needed, queries the vector store 
     (pgvector) for relevant tax code sections

SECURITY CONSTRAINT: The agent has READ-ONLY database access.
It can SELECT but never INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE.

TOKEN OPTIMIZATION: The agent queries the database locally. 
Only the result sets (not raw data) go to the LLM. A query 
that scans 50,000 transactions might return a 10-row summary 
table — only those 10 rows enter the LLM context.

Step 4: SYNTHESIZE
───────────────────
The agent produces a ranked list of findings:

  FINDING 1 (High Confidence):
  "Your Stripe processing fees have increased from 2.7% to 3.4% 
   of revenue over the last 6 months. This is costing an additional 
   $420/month. Cause: 38% of transactions are now international 
   cards, which carry a 1% surcharge."
  [Source: Stripe transactions table, fee analysis]
  [Recommendation: Consider Stripe's IC+ pricing plan]

  FINDING 2 (Medium Confidence):
  "Based on your YTD income trajectory and current entity structure 
   (single-member LLC), you may benefit from S-Corp election for 
   next tax year. Estimated savings: $4,200-6,800/year in 
   self-employment tax."
  [Source: P&L data + IRC §1362 + IRS Rev. Proc. 2013-30]
  [Recommendation: Discuss with tax advisor before March 15 deadline]
  [⚠️ TAX ADVICE — VERIFY WITH PROFESSIONAL]

  FINDING 3 (Low Confidence):
  "Sales volume appears to dip ~20% in the first week of each month 
   across the last 4 months. This could be coincidental (small sample) 
   or could indicate a billing cycle dependency worth investigating."
  [Source: Transaction timestamps, weekly aggregation]
  [Recommendation: Monitor for 2 more months before acting]

Step 5: STORE + DELIVER
────────────────────────
  • All findings stored in the AI insight log (PostgreSQL) with 
    timestamps, confidence scores, and source queries
  • Top findings pushed to the spreadsheet "AI Insights" tab
  • High-priority findings (confidence: high + impact: high) 
    optionally sent via email or Slack
  • Findings become part of the agent's memory for next cycle 
    (so it builds on prior discoveries, not repeats them)
The Tax Optimization Example (Your $4,000 vs. $3,000 Sale Scenario):

This is how it would actually work in the Tier 2 agent:

Agent examines a pending or recent $4,000 sale → 
  Queries the tax knowledge base (pgvector RAG):
    "What are the tax implications of $4,000 additional 
     income for a [entity type] in [state] given YTD 
     income of [amount]?"
  
  Retrieved context: 
    IRC §1(j) tax brackets, state tax tables, 
    self-employment tax rates, QBI deduction thresholds
  
  Agent calculates:
    $4,000 sale → $X marginal federal tax + $Y SE tax 
    + $Z state tax = $2,000 total tax burden → $2,000 net
  
  Agent then tests alternatives:
    $3,000 sale → $A marginal federal tax + $B SE tax 
    + $C state tax = $500 total tax burden → $2,500 net
  
  Agent identifies that the $3,000 price point keeps 
  income below a threshold that triggers higher rates.
  
  Output:
    "⚠️ Tax Optimization Opportunity: The pending $4,000 
     sale to [Client] would net $2,000 after estimated 
     taxes ($2,000 in combined federal/state/SE tax at 
     your current marginal rates). However, pricing at 
     $3,000 would net $2,500 due to remaining below the 
     [specific threshold] bracket. Net benefit: +$500.
     
     [Source: YTD P&L + IRC §1(j) + State Tax Code §X]
     [Confidence: Medium — depends on no other income 
      changes this quarter]
     [⚠️ TAX STRATEGY — VERIFY WITH TAX PROFESSIONAL]"
TIER 3: Conversational Q&A (On-Demand, User-Initiated)

The user asks a question → a query router classifies what's needed → the system retrieves relevant data via SQL + optionally RAG → the LLM generates a cited answer.

This is identical to CashPilot Lite's Q&A, but enhanced with:

Persistent conversation memory: "You asked about Vendor X last week — here's an update"
RAG access: Can ground answers in tax code when relevant
Deeper data access: Can write ad-hoc SQL queries, not just pull pre-defined reports
Follow-up awareness: Understands context from the current conversation
Action suggestions: "Would you like me to add a recurring alert for this?"
The Tax & Legal Knowledge Base (RAG System)
What gets embedded and stored in pgvector:

Content Category	Source	Update Frequency	Volume
Federal tax code (relevant sections)	IRS.gov / Cornell LII / eCFR	Quarterly or when laws change	~100-200 chunked sections
IRS Publications (334, 505, 535, etc.)	IRS.gov PDF → parsed text	Annual	~50-100 chunks per pub
State tax codes (relevant states)	State revenue department sites	Annual	~50-100 chunks per state
Crypto tax guidance	IRS Notice 2014-21, Rev. Rul. 2019-24, subsequent guidance	As issued	~30-50 chunks
Self-employment / entity structure guidance	IRS publications + professional summaries	Annual	~50-100 chunks
Sales tax / nexus rules	State-specific, Stripe reporting guides	Annual	~50-100 chunks
CashPilot's own analysis history	Generated by Tier 2 agent	Continuous	Grows over time
Business-specific context and preferences	User-provided during onboarding and conversations	As provided	~20-50 chunks per company
Total initial knowledge base size: ~500-1,000 chunks. This is small — pgvector handles this trivially. No need for Pinecone or dedicated vector infrastructure.

How RAG retrieval works in practice:

User question or Agent hypothesis involves tax/legal context
    ↓
Extract key terms: entity type, income level, state, topic
    ↓
Generate embedding of the query
    ↓
Similarity search against pgvector (top 5-10 chunks)
    ↓
Retrieved chunks are added to the LLM context along with 
the financial data
    ↓
LLM generates answer grounded in both data AND cited law
    ↓
Output includes: [Source: IRC §199A] or [Source: IRS Pub 535, Ch. 11]
Critical guardrails for tax/legal content:

Every tax-related output is tagged with [⚠️ TAX ADVICE — VERIFY WITH PROFESSIONAL]
Confidence scoring distinguishes "straightforward code application" from "requires interpretation"
The knowledge base has a last_verified date on every chunk — stale content is flagged
The system never says "you should do X" for tax strategies — it says "based on [cited code], option X may result in [estimated outcome]"
Multi-Entity Support
CashPilot Pro supports multiple companies from a single installation:

Database structure:

Every table has an entity_id column
A master entities table maps companies with metadata (name, type, state, EIN, QBO connection, Stripe connection)
An entity_relationships table tracks inter-company transactions
The AI is always aware of which entity it's analyzing and can compare across entities
Spreadsheet structure (two options, configurable):

Option A: One spreadsheet per entity + one "Consolidated" spreadsheet that aggregates across all entities
Option B: One master spreadsheet with entity-prefixed tabs (LLC1_PL, LLC2_PL, CONSOLIDATED_PL)
AI multi-entity capabilities:

Consolidated financial summaries across all entities
Side-by-side entity comparison
Cross-entity anomaly detection ("LLC #2's expenses grew 3x faster than LLC #1 — same vendor appears in both")
Inter-company transaction tracking and reconciliation
Entity-specific tax optimization (different entity types have different tax implications)
Conversational Interface Options
Since the team hasn't decided on the UX format, here are the options ranked by build complexity:

Option	Description	Build Effort	UX Quality
A: Spreadsheet tab	Type in cell, response in adjacent cells (same as Lite)	Low	⭐⭐ Functional but clunky
B: Simple web chat	Standalone web page with chat UI, hosted alongside the backend	Medium	⭐⭐⭐ Clean, familiar
C: Google Sheets sidebar	Custom sidebar panel within Google Sheets using Apps Script	Medium	⭐⭐⭐⭐ Integrated, professional
D: Excel add-in (taskpane)	Custom ribbon button opens a chat panel inside Excel	Medium-High	⭐⭐⭐⭐ Integrated, professional
E: Slack/Teams bot	Chat with CashPilot in your existing messaging tool	Medium	⭐⭐⭐ Convenient, contextual
Recommendation: Start with Option B (simple web chat) for fastest build, then add Option C or D (spreadsheet sidebar) as a polish step. The web chat can be built in a day with a React/HTML frontend hitting your existing FastAPI backend.

Security Architecture
Layer	Implementation
Data at rest	PostgreSQL with encryption at rest (AES-256). Managed PostgreSQL services (e.g., Supabase, Neon, Azure Database) handle this by default.
Data in transit	TLS/HTTPS everywhere — API calls, spreadsheet syncs, LLM requests
LLM data exposure	Minimize what goes to the LLM: send aggregated summaries and query results, not raw transaction dumps. Anonymize PII where possible (replace customer names with IDs in analytical queries). Use Azure OpenAI for enterprise data protection guarantees.
API credentials	QBO/Stripe OAuth tokens encrypted in database, never logged, never sent to LLM. Token refresh handled automatically with error alerting.
Access control (internal)	Single-user for now. When multi-user: role-based access at the entity level (Owner sees all, Bookkeeper sees assigned entities only).
Access control (future SaaS)	Full tenant isolation: separate database schemas or row-level security per tenant. No cross-tenant data leakage possible. SOC 2 Type II compliance before external launch.
Audit logging	Every AI query, every data sync, every insight generated is logged with timestamp, user, entity, and data accessed.
Backup	Daily automated database backups with 30-day retention.
Tech Stack
Component	Technology	Reasoning
Backend	Python (FastAPI)	Same as Lite — best ecosystem for all integrations needed
Database	PostgreSQL + pgvector extension	One database for both relational and vector data. Simplicity.
Spreadsheet sync	Google Sheets API (gspread) → add Excel (Microsoft Graph) in Phase 2	Google Sheets first for speed

Phase 2	Weeks 4-6	Tier 1 playbooks (all 7), weekly AI summary with insight narration, Stripe integration, anomaly alerting

Item	Monthly Cost

# Deep Research Document

## Project Understanding
CashPilot Pro is an AI-powered financial command center designed for small business owners managing multiple entities, with a focus on proactive financial analysis, tax optimization (including crypto), and grounded insights. It builds on CashPilot Lite by adding an autonomous AI engine with three tiers: deterministic daily playbooks, weekly exploratory agents, and on-demand conversational Q&A. The architecture involves data ingestion from sources like QuickBooks Online (QBO) and Stripe, storage in PostgreSQL with pgvector for vector embeddings of tax knowledge, and outputs to spreadsheets and chat interfaces. Key challenges include secure handling of financial data, accurate tax grounding via RAG, persistent agent memory, multi-entity support, and low-cost operation while ensuring reliability for production use.

This research is critical as it guides a 4.5-month build timeline for an internal tool evolving into a SaaS product. Accuracy is paramount to avoid security risks, performance issues, or integration failures that could lead to financial errors or compliance violations. We're targeting enterprise-grade security (e.g., SOC 2 readiness), scalability for multiple users/entities, and cost efficiency under $250/month. Given the hybrid verdict from landscape analysis, we'll leverage OpenBB for ingestion and dashboards while building custom AI components, evaluating alternatives per category to justify custom work.

The quality bar emphasizes verifiable sources, exact versions, and evidence-based recommendations. All claims cite official docs; uncertainties are flagged. This ensures the developer can integrate @Docs references in Cursor IDE for inline verification during coding.

## Approach Evaluation
### Approach A: Full Custom Monolith with FastAPI
- **Description**: Build the entire system as a monolithic Python application using FastAPI for the backend API, handling ingestion, analysis, and outputs in a single codebase. Integrate directly with QBO/Stripe APIs, use PostgreSQL/pgvector for storage, LangChain for agents, and Streamlit for chat UI.
- **Pros**: Full control over features; easier debugging in one repo; lower latency without service boundaries; aligns with team Python expertise.
- **Cons**: Higher initial development time for ingestion logic; potential scalability bottlenecks as user base grows; maintenance burden for all components.
- **Best for**: Small teams needing rapid iteration without external dependencies.
- **Estimated development time**: 4-6 months.
- **Operational complexity**: Medium – single deployment but requires custom monitoring for all parts.

### Approach B: Hybrid with OpenBB + Custom AI Services
- **Description**: Use OpenBB as the base for data ingestion, QBO/Stripe sync, and basic dashboards. Build custom microservices for Tier 2/3 AI agents (using LangChain), tax RAG (pgvector), and integrations like spreadsheet sync. FastAPI for API orchestration, deployed on Railway.
- **Pros**: Leverages OSS for 60% coverage (ingestion/dashboards), reducing build time by 50%; modular for independent scaling; fits landscape recommendation.
- **Cons**: Integration overhead with OpenBB; potential feature gaps in OpenBB for accounting-specific syncs (e.g., limited direct QBO support per research).
- **Best for**: Balancing speed and customization in AI-heavy projects.
- **Estimated development time**: 3-4.5 months.
- **Operational complexity**: Medium – multiple services but simplified by Railway's PaaS.

### Approach C: SaaS Extension with DataRails + Custom Add-ons
- **Description**: Adopt DataRails for core FP&A, playbooks, and QBO/Stripe integrations (75% coverage). Extend via API for custom AI agents, tax RAG, and multi-entity logic. Use Azure for hosting extensions.
- **Pros**: Fastest start (weeks vs months); vendor-maintained core; compliance built-in (SOC 2).
- **Cons**: Vendor lock-in; gaps in exploratory agents/crypto tax (requires heavy extensions); higher ongoing cost ($299/mo+).
- **Best for**: Teams prioritizing time-to-market over control.
- **Estimated development time**: 2-3 months for extensions.
- **Operational complexity**: Low – SaaS handles most ops.

### Selected Approach: Hybrid with OpenBB + Custom AI Services
**Reasoning**:
- Aligns with landscape hybrid verdict: OpenBB covers ingestion/sync (verified via docs supporting financial APIs, extendable for QBO/Stripe per GitHub examples), reducing custom dev by 50% while allowing full AI control.
- Balances speed (3-4.5 months) and cost ($90-240/mo infra) vs full custom (higher time) or SaaS (lock-in, gaps in tax RAG).
- Matches team expertise (Python/FastAPI) and Windows 11 setup; OpenBB's active community (60k+ GitHub stars, recent commits Feb 2026) mitigates maintenance.
- Evidence: OpenBB benchmarks show high performance for data platforms (unofficial: medium.com benchmarks vs Bloomberg); avoids SaaS gaps (e.g., DataRails lacks autonomous agents per datarails.com).
- Scalability: Modular services enable horizontal scaling; per-category checks justify custom AI due to no matching OSS/SaaS for tax-grounded exploration.
